headline: Loss eases sequentially as late-stage trial spending cools
summary_short: Viking Therapeutics posted a Q2 FY2026 net loss of $128.0M (-$1.10/share), narrowing 19.1% q/q as R&D spending eased to $115.8M from Q1's elevated VANQUISH Phase 3 enrollment costs, though the loss still widened 95.3% from $65.6M a year ago.
summary_long: R&D expenses fell to $115.8M from an elevated Q1 (down 22.9% q/q) as VANQUISH-1/2 Phase 3 enrollment activity for VK2735 wound down, though R&D still rose 92.4% y/y ($67.5M of it clinical-study costs) on the ongoing Phase 3 program. G&A rose to $16.8M (+20.5% q/q, +16.8% y/y) on higher consultant and legal costs, partly offset by lower stock-based compensation. Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments totaled $501.9M, which management says funds operations through at least September 2027. In July, the board terminated its unused $250M repurchase authorization and approved a new $500M program. Ligand is separately disputing Viking's license to the VK2809/VK0214 TR-Beta program in pending litigation. No revenue, EPS, or expense guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Y/y increase driven by $67.5M higher clinical-study costs for the VANQUISH-1/2 Phase 3 trials, plus salaries (+$1.3M) and stock comp (+$1.1M), partly offset by lower manufacturing (-$10.3M) and preclinical (-$4.7M) spend.
Y/y increase driven by higher third-party consultants (+$3.9M) and legal/patent services (+$1.4M), partly offset by lower stock-based compensation (-$3.5M).

Cash and short-term investments of $501.9M are said to fund operations into September 2027; Ligand separately disputes Viking's license to the TR-Beta program.
